question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool feature now, or require the broader federation identity/scope contract before adding core cross-gateway messaging?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses Gateway trust boundaries and likely adds config, protocol, credentials, and message-delivery semantics that current docs and role policy do not define.

options.title: Design federation contract first
options.body: Require a maintainer-approved peer identity, scope, credential, audit, and session-state contract before merging a core cross-gateway session primitive.

options.title: Repair the narrow peer PR
options.body: Allow the linked PR or a replacement to proceed if it preserves the boundary model and proves fresh-install plus upgrade behavior across two real Gateways.

options.title: Defer to plugins or MCP bridges
options.body: Keep core session tools local-only for now and document supported external bridge patterns until a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design federation contract first
recommendation.body: Require a maintainer-approved peer identity, scope, credential, audit, and session-state contract before merging a core cross-gateway session primitive.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans gateway role policy, session protocol evolution, and recent broad session management changes that define the trust boundary.
